Senses.Explanation: This is the named third member of Deshan Yuanming's three phrases, not merely an instruction to move with water. The underlying scene is motion that keeps going with successive waves and swells. Deshan sets it after 'enclosing heaven and earth' and 'cutting off the many streams' and asks the assembly to distinguish the three. A reviewed unnamed monk asks Ruiyan Zhicai what the phrase of following the waves is; Guyun Quan applies following the waves and cutting off the streams when appraising Xuefeng Yicun's and Zhaozhou Congshen's earlier answers; Yuantong Faxiu says that trimming a sail to the wind is precisely following the waves, then immediately takes up cutting off the streams. These named uses establish a recognized phrase inside a transmitted three-part set without supplying one unrecorded universal meaning.
Senses.Note: Deshan Yuanming, an heir of Yunmen Wenyan, is the source-attested speaker of the three-phrase formulation; it must not be attributed to Yunmen himself. Six allowlisted texts carry Deshan's address. A reviewed unnamed monk's recurring question to Ruiyan Zhicai—'what is the phrase of following the waves?'—independently confirms that the wording functions as a named phrase. The ordinary predicate is kept as a different sense below.

Occurrences.Kwic: 函葢乾坤，一句截斷眾流，一句隨波逐浪。作麼生辯？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps, volumes 10–25 (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)), Deshan Yuanming section. Deshan Yuanming tells the assembly that he has three phrases, lists enclosing heaven and earth, cutting off the many streams, and following the waves, then asks how they are distinguished.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如何是隨波逐浪句？師曰：隨。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps, volumes 10–25 (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)), Ruiyan Zhicai section. An unnamed monk asks what the phrase of following the waves is; Ruiyan Zhicai answers, 'Follow.' All six attribution rungs leave the questioner personally unnamed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰：一人隨波逐浪，一人截斷眾流。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continuation and Abridgement of the Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元續略), Guyun Quan section. Guyun Quan raises Xuefeng Yicun's and Zhaozhou Congshen's answers about the ancient ravine's cold spring and says one follows the waves while the other cuts off the many streams.

Occurrences.Kwic: 看風使帆，正是隨波逐浪。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps, volumes 10–25 (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)), Yuantong Faxiu section. Yuantong Faxiu says trimming the sail to the wind is precisely following the waves and then appraises cutting off the many streams.

AlternateTargets: following the waves, chasing the swells
Senses.Explanation: To follow wave after wave is to keep moving as successive waves and swells carry the course. Qingshan Neng uses the water image as an ordinary predicate after seeing forms and hearing sounds and before revolving through the three realms; Songxi Ziding rebukes spending all day following the waves and generating needless branches; Shiyu Mingfang says that from youth he followed them while foolish and ignorant. These named contexts are critical, but they do not make every use a technical teaching or prescribe the opposite action.
Senses.Note: Qingshan Neng, Songxi Ziding, and Shiyu Mingfang independently attest the ordinary predicate in three lamp records. Yuantong Faxiu's sail-trimming equation immediately handles the paired phrase 'cutting off the many streams,' so his occurrence belongs to the named-phrase sense rather than this ordinary predicate.

Occurrences.Kwic: 見色聞聲，隨波逐浪，流轉
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Orthodox Pulse of the Chan Lineage (禪宗正脉), Qingshan Neng section. Qingshan Neng says that beings who see forms and hear sounds follow wave after wave, revolve through the three realms, and sink among the four modes of birth.

Occurrences.Kwic: 終日隨波逐浪、妄生枝節者哉
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Orthodox Succession of the Continued Lamp (續燈正統), Songxi Ziding section. Songxi Ziding contrasts Bodhidharma's single mechanism with people who spend all day following wave after wave and needlessly generating branches.

Occurrences.Kwic: 明芳愚懦無知，自少隨波逐浪。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Shiyu Mingfang section. Shiyu Mingfang names himself in the line and says that, foolish and ignorant, from youth he followed wave after wave.
